rows.question: Have you checked whether Tool A already has a dashboard, saved report, export or integration that would produce the status report with no manual work?
rows.note: answer: no export can produce the client-mandated spreadsheet

rows.question: When someone in your team last spent a long time on a report, was the cause the tool's limits or something else, such as unclear task ownership?
rows.note: cause of long reporting is copying into the client spreadsheet

rows.question: Could part of the reporting be removed altogether, for example by sending fewer or shorter reports, instead of making them faster?
rows.note: reducing report count; mandated format and copying not clearly stated

rows.question: Would the people who read your status reports accept a link to a live dashboard in place of the document or meeting they get now?
rows.note: readers require a client-mandated spreadsheet format

rows.question: In a typical reporting week, how many of the hours go to pulling data out of Tool A versus chasing teammates to update their tasks?
rows.note: time breakdown shows most goes to copying into the client spreadsheet

rows.question: Which person on the team could spend an hour or two a week keeping Tool B in order, and have they agreed to it?
Does any security, privacy or data-location requirement of your company apply to a new tool, and has Tool B been approved for it?
If three of the people who complain most about Tool A build this week's status report in Tool B using real project data, how much time does it take them compared with today?
rows.note: trial in Tool B; no hidden fact directly stated

rows.question: When does your Tool A contract renew, and how much notice must you give to leave?
rows.note: renewal date reveals the auto-renewal with no refund

rows.question: Besides seat price, what other costs would differ between the tools, such as add-ons, storage, integrations or support tiers?
